prize_parts.citation: for empirical and conceptual analysis of how technology and import competition reshape labour demand, wages and local labour markets

statement.case_for: I opened with B042 first and B032 second, and after reading the colleagues' openings I now prefer B032 as the single proposed achievement. It rests on a credibly identified body of evidence with transparent research designs. Local labour-market exposure to import competition, combined with a task-based account of technology, changed how economists and policymakers think about who gains and loses from trade and automation. The core papers are 10 to 20 years old, have been replicated, re-examined and extended, and their main qualitative conclusions have survived scrutiny while magnitudes and persistence remain debated. That combination of originality, evidential credibility and lasting influence meets the common criteria I would apply to any field. It is also the only shortlisted candidate that every one of my colleagues ranked in their top eight, but I treat that as a weak signal and not as scientific merit. The reason I move it ahead of B042 is that Dreber and Hjalmarsson make the maturity case convincingly. Their point is that the findings have been tested and have held, whereas the collateral-channel mechanism in B042 is more influential as theory than directly validated. I propose Autor, Hanson and Dorn because the China-shock design and its local-labour-market evidence are the most clearly identifiable credited unit, and all three are core authors of it.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the main weakness. The task-based framework is shared with scholars outside this ballot (Acemoglu, Levy, Murnane) and with Katz, who is inside it. Any three-person cut therefore leaves out a real contributor: Katz if I choose Dorn, Dorn if I choose Katz. The conceptual half of the contribution is thus only partly captured by the credited names. The shift-share exposure designs have faced inference and external-validity criticism, and the aggregate and long-run magnitudes of the trade shock are still contested. There is also thematic proximity to the 2024 prize on technology and institutions, and to recent labour-market prizes (Card and Angrist, Goldin). A committee that wants a clean, theory-anchored mechanism with a tight two-person credit line, as in B042, has a reasonable case.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranked B032 first with Autor, Hanson and Katz, treating it as a conceptual task framework plus quasi-experimental evidence whose main conclusions have held up. She also flagged that a three-person cap forces Dorn out, a real judgement call.
responses.response: I agree on maturity and on the pairing of concept and evidence, and her argument pushed me toward B032. I differ on the third name. My opening included Katz, but the credited unit I can attribute most cleanly is the China-shock design, where Dorn is a core co-author and Katz is not. The task-framework credit is shared with people outside the list in any case, so adding Katz does not make that half of the contribution complete. I therefore switch to Dorn, while acknowledging that Katz's work on the skill premium is foundational and that this is a close call.

responses.point: Dreber ranked B032 first because of its transparent empirical designs, replication and re-examination, and policy influence. She regards the debate over magnitude and persistence as compatible with being mature enough to rank first.
responses.response: I largely agree and have partly adopted her reasoning. Transparent designs that have survived re-examination are the criterion I weigh most heavily. I would qualify her two-person proposal of Autor and Hanson only on attribution: omitting Dorn understates a co-author who is central to the local-labour-market papers. I also do not treat the first-place rankings as strengthening the case. The case has to rest on the evidence and the unresolved exposure-design critiques.

responses.point: Enflo ranked B042 third. She sees the Kiyotaki-Moore credit-cycles paper as the clear origin of the collateral amplification mechanism, with tight two-person credit. She cautions that the committee may want an empirical anchor and that the 2022 financial-intermediation prize could be read as either complementary or redundant.
responses.response: I accept the attribution point; that is why B042 was my first choice and remains my first alternative. I now weight her empirical-anchor reservation more heavily than I did in my opening. The theoretical influence is large, but direct identification of the collateral channel is mixed. The 2022 overlap also cuts against B042 in a way it does not cut against B032. I do not think Gertler's inclusion, as Hjalmarsson and Strömberg propose, resolves this, since it brings the accelerator lineage and Bernanke's earlier recognition back into the credit question.

responses.point: Krusell ranked B014 first. He argues that nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary policy, that the contribution is mature and arguably overdue, and that Calvo, Taylor and Woodford are the foundational trio even though Gali, Gertler and Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans have strong claims.
responses.response: I do not dispute B014's importance for practice, and leaving it out of my own top eight reflects my difficulty with attribution rather than a judgement on merit. With eight credited names and several equally strong claimants, any three-person selection is contestable in a way that Autor, Hanson and Dorn on the China-shock design is less so. I would also want the committee to say explicitly how it reads the post-2021 inflation debate before treating the framework as settled. I leave B014 outside my alternatives because I cannot defend a particular trio.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the task-based framework and the trade-shock evidence as one contribution, and how to credit Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane, who are outside the ballot or already recognised.
Dorn versus Katz for the third place: the choice is sensitive and I have changed it from my opening.
How much weight the persistence and magnitude critiques of shift-share exposure designs should carry in judging maturity.
Whether the 2024 prize and other recent labour-market recognition make B032 less timely than B042 or B016.
I rely on my own knowledge of the literature and have not independently verified citation counts or attribution details.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent for B032 from the supplied profile. My research field (comparative democratisation, quality of government, V-Dem) is adjacent to B016, and my 2024 presentation speech concerned institutions and prosperity. That speech may reflect collective drafting and does not establish a personal prize preference. The profile documents no collaboration with Persson, Tabellini or Besley. Hassler's opening places Persson at the IIES, and my profile notes IIES colleagues at Stockholm University in a different department, so there is institutional proximity to B016, which I list only as an alternative. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
